feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy-focused roles. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive, light on outcome metrics in places, and slightly over-structured with overlapping skills sections.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within the same organization strongly support leadership growth and trust.  
- Good impact signals: website scale, audience size, platform migration, studio buildout, and analytics stack all add substance.  
- Writing is professional and readable, with strong domain vocabulary and a consistent strategic tone.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve focus and save space.  
- Add sharper results where possible: several bullets describe responsibilities well but would be stronger with outcomes (e.g., traffic growth, engagement lifts, efficiency gains, campaign results).  
- Fix minor style/grammar consistency issues: use “12 years of experience” instead of “12 years experience”; standardize serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “workflows and systems”); “front-end”/“organization-wide” hyphenation is good, but punctuation around bullets in paragraph form feels inconsistent. No obvious misspellings or major typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro that aligns well with the CV, but it reads a bit generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening it and adding one or two concrete signals of seniority would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Replace broad phrases like “expert in” with sharper, evidence-backed positioning tied to recent work: digital strategy, CMS modernization, analytics, and governance.
- Reduce the long channel list; group it as “multi-channel” to avoid sounding repetitive.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving web, content, email, social, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Specializes in cross-channel strategy, CMS modernization, digital governance, and workflow design that improve coordination, publishing efficiency, and audience engagement. Brings deep experience in advocacy communications, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “workflow/systems,” and “stakeholder coordination” are repeated in Core Competencies and Soft Skills.
- “Mission-driven organizations” and advocacy messaging also recur in later sections; keep the intro high-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership/strategy capabilities will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and pluralize for consistency: “Multi-channel communications,” “Web platform & CMS administration,” “Analytics & performance reporting.”
- Prioritize senior, differentiating strengths first: digital transformation, editorial/governance systems, web platform leadership, analytics, stakeholder coordination.
- Replace vague wording like “Workflow & systems architecture” with clearer CV language such as “Content operations & workflow architecture” or “Digital governance & workflow design.”
- Suggested rewrite: Digital transformation & platform modernization • Multi-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS administration • Editorial governance & workflow design • Analytics & performance reporting • Content operations & systems architecture • Cross-functional stakeholder coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and the header.
- “Multi-channel communication” and “Policy & advocacy communication” repeat language already covered in the header and Topline Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a service list rather than a high-impact recent position. Tighten around 3–5 outcomes-focused bullets and make the scope/results clearer.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client type + remit: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital strategy, Drupal platform improvements, content operations, and campaign delivery.”
- Rewrite bullets to emphasize ownership and outcomes: “Built cross-functional workflows, analytics, and publishing systems to improve coordination across organization-wide communications.”
- Combine overlapping web/CMS lines: “Designed and implemented Drupal campaign experiences, including microsites, modular content components, downloadable toolkits, and front-end enhancements for high-traffic public web properties.”
- Keep the AI/search work as the strongest differentiator: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval strategy, structured content design, and user-facing discovery experience.” Add metrics if possible (traffic, publishers, time saved, engagement lift).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Governance, analytics, and enterprise web modernization overlap with the NACo Director role; focus this entry on current consulting impact, Drupal builds, and AI search.
- “Campaign/storytelling experiences” overlaps with Recent Projects; avoid repeating project details verbatim.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening were tighter and the bullets emphasized outcomes, team/operational scope, and what changed under your leadership.

Suggested edit
- Replace the broad opener with a results-led summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Tighten and front-load impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable outcomes where missing: growth in email/social engagement, reduced production costs/timelines from the studio, reporting adoption, or governance efficiency gains.
- Make bullets more executive-level by using stronger verbs and fewer lists: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring multimedia content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Email newsletters, video programming, and workflow improvements overlap with the prior NACo role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, platform modernization, analytics, and governance.
- “Governance/publishing standards/planning systems” may duplicate the freelance role; distinguish this as organization-wide operational transformation.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but this entry reads generic and overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Tighten it around scope, channel ownership, and concrete operational impact.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize ownership and scale: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Make bullets more outcome-oriented: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders” and, if possible, add open rates, growth, or send volume.
- Strengthen the video bullet with a result: “Launched/expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.” Add cadence, views, or audience growth if available.
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper operations bullet: “Improved editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, increasing consistency and cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital publishing workflows” and “editorial coordination” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning language.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this item as scaling/formalizing the program, not starting it.

- Editorial governance and content operations

- “Multi-channel communications leadership” overlaps with both recent NACo roles and Core Competencies’ “Multi-channel communications operations.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT” and reads as a raw tool list rather than a senior, impact-oriented skills summary. In this section, emphasize platform leadership and execution themes tied to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS delivery • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal first and consider dropping one lower-priority platform if space is tight; it is the most supported by recent experience.
- Replace “Power Pages” and “SharePoint” with broader value language only if those tools are not central to target roles.
- If possible, add scale in adjacent experience bullets rather than here (e.g., 10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates the “Technical + IT” section; keep Topline Skills higher-level and reserve full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” also overlap with Core Competencies.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

items.aiFeedback:

- Executive and leadership reporting

- If possible, align wording with recent experience impact: “analytics infrastructure,” “executive reporting,” “performance optimization.”

- This largely duplicates “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; keep Topline Skills higher-level and leave full tool inventory there.
- “Leadership reporting” overlaps with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies; use one phrasing consistently.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Since Drupal is central to recent roles, this item should either sharpen platform depth or be consolidated.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider adding level/context to show depth: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites, governance) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, make Drupal more outcome-linked: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; 3.5M annual page views)**
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; avoid listing platforms here if they’re not meaningfully used in recent work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one section or using this item for platform depth while leaving the other broader.
- **GitHub Pages** may feel lightweight versus the seniority of the CV unless tied to a specific use case.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation depth and newer tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from basic languages to applied capability: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versions consistently elsewhere.
- Consider replacing “Google Tag Manager” with “Tag management” if you want this item to stay implementation-focused and avoid overlap with analytics.
- If accurate, add one outcome-oriented qualifier in parentheses, e.g., “API integrations (CMS, analytics, campaign tools)” or “GitHub Actions (build/deploy workflows).”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills: “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations • Workflow automation.”
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under “Data, Analytics & Optimization” than coding/implementation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere, so tighten and frame around implementation value.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Group by function for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Team collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If accurate, add scope/context instead of just names, e.g. “Used to build editorial planning systems, automate approvals/notifications, and coordinate cross-team publishing workflows.”
- Consider dropping weaker/older tools if not recent; prioritize Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, Teams.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” already appears under Topline Skills; avoid repeating Airtable as a headline differentiator in both places unless this section adds context.
- “Workflow automation” is already named in Core Competencies and Web Platforms & Technical Execution; this item should list tools concisely, not restate the theme.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this item is too generic and underplays your stronger, recent email leadership in NACo roles. It should signal scale/use case, not just list platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten and order by likely relevance/recency: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in brief parentheticals: **Higher Logic (newsletter/member communications)** • **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey automation/segmentation)** • **Mailchimp (campaign email)**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, consider featuring only 1–2 tools here and letting work experience carry the scale/impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with repeated “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” in Work Experience; avoid restating audience size here unless tied to a platform-specific achievement.
- “Engagement Systems” is vague and may duplicate broader “Multi-channel communications operations” language elsewhere.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid progression story, but this reads broadly and overlaps with the stronger, more recent NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with clearer scope and any available metrics.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website traffic, livestream/event volume, video cadence, email frequency, or audience growth.
- Tighten the second sentence to highlight distinct contributions: “Supported a major website refresh, produced livestreams and weekly video updates, and improved day-to-day publishing workflows.”
- Replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with a stronger management verb if accurate: “supervised,” “mentored,” or “trained” a digital media associate.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the later “weekly advocacy video update”; keep this entry broader/foundational unless this was a distinct series.
- Workflow/process language also appears in later NACo roles, so avoid repeating “strengthening workflows” without a specific example or result.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed around outcomes so it complements—rather than repeats—the later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize ownership and firsts: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county policy and program priorities.”
- Separate digital/media contribution into a stronger impact line: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational communications, translating research and policy work into audience-facing materials.”
- Make the podcast achievement the anchor: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add one measurable result: number of episodes launched, audience/downloads, stakeholder groups served, or programs/policy initiatives supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid broad “digital content production” phrasing if later roles already cover multimedia; keep this entry focused on innovation/research support plus the podcast first.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here, since leadership is more credibly established in the 2015–2024 NACo roles.
